issues.description: Duplicated mode->bytes derivation between sign_message and verify_signature
issues.detail: The new chia/wallet/util/signing.py centralizes signing, but the mode-to-message-bytes derivation (CHIP_0002_HEX_INPUT vs CHIP_0002 vs BLS_*_UTF8/HEX) is still implemented twice — once in sign_message() and once (with slightly different ordering) in verify_signature(). The refactor's central invariant ought to be that signed bytes == verified bytes for every SigningMode. Extract a single canonical_message_bytes(mode, message) helper used by both paths so the invariant is enforced by construction, not by code review.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum mapping is non-exhaustive and silently falls through
issues.detail: signing_mode_enum() in wallet_request_types.py uses an if/elif chain over the four (is_hex, safe_mode) combinations, then falls through to CHIP_0002 for the remaining case (not is_hex and safe_mode). The truth table would be clearer and provably exhaustive as a dict lookup keyed by (is_hex, safe_mode) returning the four SigningMode values, or at least with the final case labeled `else: # not is_hex and safe_mode` so the reader does not have to deduce the missing row. As written, a future fifth case could silently land in CHIP_0002.

issues.description: verify_signature docstring still references nonexistent `request` parameter
issues.detail: The docstring on the new free-standing verify_signature() reads `:param request:` / `:return:` — a copy-paste residue from when it was an RPC handler taking a single request object. The function now takes keyword args (signing_mode, public_key, message, signature, address). A literate-programming-grade comment here should describe each parameter and, importantly, the address-binding semantics (CHIP_0002_P2_DELEGATED_CONDITIONS uses the raw pubkey puzzle; other modes use the synthetic-key puzzle hash) so a reader does not need to run the code to understand the contract.

issues.description: Misleading variable name `hex_message` for non-hex inputs
issues.detail: Inside sign_message() the local is called `hex_message` even on the UTF-8 path (`hex_message = bytes(message, "utf-8")`) and on the CHIP-0002 tree-hash path. The name encodes a false invariant. Rename to `message_to_sign` (matching `message_to_verify` in verify_signature) so the two halves of the same scheme use the same vocabulary. Small, but exactly the kind of readability fix the refactor was an opportunity to make.

issues.description: convert_secret_key_to_synthetic lives on Wallet but is conceptually a free function
issues.detail: `Wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic(self, secret_key)` does not touch self. It is a pure function of secret_key and DEFAULT_HIDDEN_PUZZLE_HASH, and it is now invoked from the RPC layer as `self.service.wallet_state_manager.main_wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic(...)` — a long indirection for something with no state dependency. Either make it a @staticmethod, or move it into chia/wallet/util/signing.py alongside sign_message so all synthetic-key derivation lives in one place. As written it is harmless but ill-placed.

issues.description: sign_message_by_id calls signing_mode_enum three times for the same request
issues.detail: In wallet_rpc_api.sign_message_by_id, `request.signing_mode_enum` is invoked once for the sign call, once for the response, and (per pattern) again for the value field — and the same in sign_message_by_address. The property recomputes the if/elif chain each call. Trivial cost, but the literate version names it once at the top of the handler: `mode = request.signing_mode_enum` and uses `mode` throughout, which also documents that all three sites refer to the same mode value.

issues.description: Test asserts BLS verification but does not assert signing_mode in response
issues.detail: test_sign_message_by_nft_id verifies the BLS signature directly but does not assert that response.signing_mode reflects the requested (is_hex, safe_mode) combination. Since this PR's whole point is centralizing mode derivation, a one-line assert per case (`assert response.signing_mode == SigningMode.X.value`) would lock in the truth table that signing_mode_enum() encodes and catch any future regression in the fall-through case.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED / NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT. The refactor is structurally sound — pulling sign/verify into chia/wallet/util/signing.py is the right move, and centralizing the (is_hex, safe_mode) -> SigningMode mapping removes real duplication from the RPC handlers. But the new module misses the opportunity to enforce the most important invariant of a signing library by construction: signed bytes equals verified bytes for every mode. That mapping still appears twice, in two different orderings, in the same file. Secondary issues are readability residue from the move (stale `:param request:` docstring, `hex_message` name on non-hex paths, a stateless method left on Wallet, repeated property calls in handlers) and a missing test assertion on signing_mode that would lock the truth table. None are correctness-blocking; together they are the difference between a refactor that ships and one that audits.
